Thanks for the ping — quick summary from Legal on marketplace entitlements and billing:

- Azure private plans typically require that SaaS entitlements delivered through the marketplace be invoiced via Microsoft when those entitlements are the primary product. However, it is common and acceptable to separately invoice professional services (one-time) directly to the customer, provided the SOW clearly separates PS line items from SaaS subscription fees.

- License eligibility: our standard private plan licensing covers both internal and external-facing usage unless the customer is materially reselling the service or embedding our models in a product that they resell as a separate offering. For customer-facing features that effectively become a product for resale, we need to evaluate additional licensing language / revenue share.

- Action items for HorizonTech to expedite:
  1) Separate the SOW into discrete SaaS subscription rows (marketplace) vs PS rows (direct invoice).
  2) Provide PO numbers and the legal billing address for direct invoices.
  3) Confirm if any portion of usage will be redistributed/resold by HorizonTech — if "yes" we need an IP/revenue discussion.

I recommend we loop in the MSFT marketplace contact to validate the entitlement flow; I can do a short call and surface any contract exhibit changes (DPA/DP processing language).
